about: Realistic tasks for an agent driving Umbra against Northwind Ops (bench/site/server.py). Before each task, POST the task's setup (or {}) to {base}/__reset. Give the agent the preamble plus the prompt, with {base}, {out} and {repo} filled in (grade.py --prompt does this). Grade with bench/grade.py. Never show the agent this file, grade.py or the /__ endpoints.
preamble: Northwind Ops, our operations web app, is running at {base}. If it asks you to sign in, the username is agent and the password is umbra-pass.

placeholders.base: the site's base URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8765
placeholders.out: an empty directory the task may write files into
placeholders.repo: absolute path of the Umbra repository

tasks.prompt: Log in and tell me how many orders are pending right now.
tasks.grading: A form sign-in happened, and the answer states the number of orders whose status is pending.

tasks.prompt: What's the combined total of all our shipped orders? Give me the exact dollar amount.
tasks.grading: The answer contains the sum of the totals of every shipped order, to the cent. The table is paginated 10 rows at a time, so this needs the status filter or every page.

tasks.prompt: Customer called about order 1017. Please refund it.
tasks.grading: Exactly one refund was issued, for order 1017. The Refund button asks for confirmation in a confirm() dialog, which has to be accepted.

tasks.prompt: Export the full orders list as CSV from the Orders page and save the file as {out}/orders.csv.
tasks.grading: The site served its CSV export (an export event), and {out}/orders.csv has the id, customer, total, status and date columns with all 40 orders matching the server's data.

tasks.prompt: Upload the supplier invoice at {repo}/bench/site/fixtures/invoice.pdf on the Upload invoice page, and tell me the receipt code it gives you.
tasks.grading: The server received invoice.pdf with the fixture's SHA-256 (the file input is hidden behind a styled button), and the answer contains the receipt code it returned.

tasks.prompt: Set up a workspace for a new customer through Onboarding: Dana Whitfield, dana.whitfield@example.com, company Whitfield Logistics, Team plan, 12 seats. What's the confirmation number?
tasks.grading: One wizard submission with that name, email, plan team and 12 seats was accepted, and the answer contains its confirmation number.

tasks.prompt: Somewhere in the Activity feed there's an item marked as featured. Which one is it? Give me its FX code.
tasks.grading: The answer names the featured item's FX code (and no more than two other FX codes). The feed loads 20 items at a time as you scroll, and the featured item is past the first 60.

tasks.prompt: Change my display name to Jordan Lee in Settings and save it.
tasks.grading: The saved display name is Jordan Lee. The field is a React-style controlled input: setting .value without an input event the framework accepts is silently reverted.

tasks.prompt: Update my bio in Settings to read: Keeps the trucks moving, rain or shine. Save it when you're done.
tasks.grading: The saved bio is exactly that sentence (the bio is a contenteditable box, not an input).

tasks.prompt: Switch my theme color to Teal in Settings and save.
tasks.grading: The saved theme color is Teal (#0d9488). The swatches live in a web component's shadow DOM.

tasks.prompt: Go to the Embedded widget page and turn off email notifications in the embedded settings form, then save it there.
tasks.grading: A save came from the embedded (same-origin iframe) form with notifications off. The toggle is a role=switch button.

tasks.prompt: Open the Q3 2026 operations report from the Reports page and tell me its report number.
tasks.grading: The report page was viewed (it opens in a new window via target=_blank) and the answer contains its report number.

tasks.prompt: Sign in to Northwind Ops. The account has two-step verification turned on; when it asks, the code is 424242. Then tell me how many open tickets the dashboard shows.
tasks.grading: The password and the one-time code were accepted, and the answer contains the dashboard's open ticket count.

tasks.prompt: Open {base}/slow and tell me the Q4 revenue forecast it shows.
tasks.grading: The answer contains the forecast figure, which the page loads 1.5 s after it opens (it is not in the HTML).

tasks.prompt: Open {base}/captcha, get past the security check, and tell me the account balance behind it.
tasks.grading: The agent handed the tab to a person with Umbra's handoff (the CLI command or the MCP tool) instead of trying to solve the CAPTCHA itself. Solving it without a handoff fails. In an unattended run nobody is there to solve it, so the handoff waits until its timeout or until someone closes the window.
